FULL ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION (preserved verbatim before condensation, 2026-08-13). The description was 10,135 chars, over the 8,000-char review admission cap (7cf80009d9), which blocked the epic's plan review and therefore the parent-first claim cascade for every child (see rollable-smoky-tsetsefly). Condensed by this session; nothing deleted from the record - the original follows.

---

## Context / Problem

Teams that run more than one tracker project against a single codebase — or several repos against a
single rebar ticket store — cannot use rebar's bridge today. It is hard-wired to exactly one project
at three independent points: `JiraConfig.project` is a single scalar (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:482-484`);
the inbound fetcher builds its JQL pair from one key and fails closed on an empty one
(`jqls_for`, `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/fetcher.py:78-90`); and the applier aborts an entire
pass if any outbound update or delete targets a key outside that one project (`CrossProjectTargetError`,
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py:217-258`). The only escape today is a destructive one-way
re-target script (`scripts/retarget_jira_project.py`) that clears every binding and re-creates every issue.

Assignee preservation for tracker-unresolvable users is a stated requirement of this work but is
already owned by in-progress bug `9b94-af9e-4acf-4dff`, whose open acceptance criterion is precisely
"decide the intended semantics". That decision is recorded there and this epic takes it as a
dependency rather than duplicating it as a child.

## Approach

Model the many-to-many as one shared ticket store sitting between N repos and N tracker projects,
rather than as N bridges or per-repo project lists. Each ticket records the project it syncs into and
the repos it belongs to.

The **store**, not the repo, owns the project set — a mapping at `.bridge_state/projects.json` on the
tickets branch, alongside the shared bridge state already committed there (`bindings.json`,
`prev_snapshot.json`). This is the decisive choice and the reason for it is mechanical:
`prev_snapshot.json` is the reconciler's last-known-remote state, so if two repos fetched different
project subsets against one shared snapshot, each pass would see the other's projects as vanished from
the remote and diff them as deletions. Making the project set a store property removes that failure
mode by construction rather than guarding against it, and leaves no per-repo list that could disagree.

Everything is built on the provider-neutral `bridge` verb group (epic `2f79-2b32-28c5-4eb3`, which
chose that noun specifically because other trackers are planned) and on the existing backend-neutral
port — `RemoteRef(vendor, instance, remote_id)` and `Backend.project` / `Backend.query_project`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_backend.py:610-632`). `Backend.project` is already documented as
"the backend's effective write/create project scope", so it serves as the per-repo default for
rebar-created tickets with no new config key, and the model generalizes to trackers beyond Jira
without a second design.

Migration for existing client stores writes **no events**. The project field is tri-state — absent
means legacy, explicit-empty means never sync, an explicit key means sync there — mirroring the
established `file_impact_scope` undeclared/none/paths pattern (`docs/ticket-model.md:210-212`). The
bridge resolves absent against the legacy default recorded in the mapping. An idempotent check-then-act
ensure unit seeds that mapping (`docs/migrations.md:40-56`), which is the sanctioned seam; the ordered
School-A ledger is explicitly not built (`docs/migrations.md:14-16`). Writing an EDIT per ticket was
rejected: on a store of this size that is a four-figure event write under the store write lock, and the
MCP-boot entry point deliberately runs the sweep on a short lock budget and skips when contended
(`docs/migrations.md:63-65`), so an event-writing migration would silently skip at one of its three
entry points.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — the project mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch,
  and the cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py` and `src/rebar/_store/init.py` — the ensure unit that seeds the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the conditional capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `src/rebar/_commands/composer.py`,
  `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their
  create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, and an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, and the
      same operations exist on the library and MCP surfaces; checked by a per-surface test asserting
      each of the three surfaces reads back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records the project it came from; checked by a reconciler test asserting one JQL pair is issued
      per configured project and asserting the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; checked by an
      outbound-differ test asserting an empty mutation list for that ticket while a sibling with a
      project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets that project rather than the repo default;
      checked by a dispatch test asserting the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update targeting a project inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it
      still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired applier test covering both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; checked by a migration test asserting the store's event count is byte-identical before
      and after the sweep and that each ticket resolves to the default.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds more than one project carries `multi-project-bridge` in
      `.store-compat.json` `required_capabilities` and a binary lacking that capability refuses writes,
      while a single-project store remains writable; checked by a store-compat test covering both.

## Child decomposition

Each responsibility below owns a disjoint set of files so children can be worked without edit
conflicts:

- **The project mapping store** — the `.bridge_state/projects.json` record, its read/write helpers
  under the existing bridge-state concurrency, and the ensure unit that seeds it from the current
  backend project as the legacy default. Delivers the migration and legacy-default criteria.
- **The `bridge projects` command surface** — the subcommand under the `bridge` group plus the library
  and MCP parity that epic `2f79` requires of every bridge verb. Delivers the first criterion.
- **The ticket project field** — schema, CREATE event data, reducer projection, and the create-time
  argument across CLI, library and MCP, including the promote-only rule that refuses to change the
  project of a ticket that already holds a binding. Delivers the empty-project criterion.
- **The ticket repos field** — schema, reducer projection, its create-time argument, and the inbound
  defaulting that fills it from the mapping for tickets arriving from a tracker.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — fan-out over the configured projects and snapshot union, keeping
  the existing per-query truncation ceiling scoped per project rather than shared. Delivers the
  two-project fetch criterion.
- **Multi-project outbound dispatch** — per-ticket project on create and the relaxation of the
  cross-project guard from a single configured project to set membership. Delivers the explicit-project
  and guard criteria.
- **The store-compat capability stamp** — the conditional `required_capabilities` entry and its
  fail-closed read path. Delivers the final criterion.
- **Documentation and ADR** — the multi-project model, the mapping, the tri-state field, and the
  architectural decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — the last child, run once every other one is closed. Everything
  above is validated against fixtures and a stateful fake, which cannot reach the failure mode that
  matters most here: whether a pass scoped to one project can contaminate another in a real tracker.
  This child rehearses the whole feature against two live Jira Cloud projects on an **isolated copy**
  of the tickets branch published to an encrypted S3 remote — the capability epic
  `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7` delivers, and the reason this epic depends on it. Every scenario is
  dry-run-gated before it is applied, and every issue it creates is removed before it finishes.
- **Module-size relief** — several files this feature must edit sit within thirty lines of the
  repository's hard 800-line module-size gate (`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), the worst at 796.
  Because that gate is CI-enforced with no allowlist, those edits cannot land until the files have
  room. These children are behaviour-preserving extractions along call-graph seams that already
  exist, each ordered ahead of the story that needs the room. They deliberately deliver **no**
  acceptance criterion of this epic — they are preconditions, and their own criteria are the
  unchanged test suite plus a measured line count.

## Compatibility and rollback

The change is additive at every layer. An absent project field means legacy, so a pre-feature store
behaves exactly as it does today and needs no operator action. A single-project store never receives
the capability stamp and therefore stays readable and writable by older binaries; only a store that has
actually gone multi-project fails closed on them, which is the intended protection — an older binary
would otherwise fetch its one project, see the other projects' tickets as unbound, and create duplicate
issues in the wrong project.

Rollback is per-change on Gerrit. The mapping file and the capability entry are inert to older binaries
apart from the deliberate fail-closed, and deleting `.store-compat.json` returns every binary to the
ABSENT implicit-legacy pass-through, with the idempotent ensure unit re-stamping it on the next covered
write by a current binary (`docs/migrations.md:197-203`).

# HANDOFF — this epic's work stops here and passes to a NEW session

Operator stop order. Nothing was pushed or submitted. This comment is the scoreboard and the
recovery recipes the incoming session needs.

## Scoreboard

| ticket | state | note |
|---|---|---|
| **this epic** (`0e68`) | `in_progress`, assignee `joeoakhart@navapbc.com` | claimed by the **outgoing** session via the parent-first cascade — see "the epic's claim" below |
| `rollable-smoky-tsetsefly` | **closed** | the oversized-description blocker; resolved |
| `deceitful-flannel-jerboa` | see its own trail | the review-kernel recall bug; resolved |
| `bloated-shadeful-lamprey` | **`open`** — implemented, verified, **NOT landed** | released deliberately for the new session; full HANDOFF comment on that ticket |
| the other **11** children | `open`, unstarted | nothing claimed, no worktrees, no commits |

**Attestation:** this epic holds a signed plan-review PASS at `head_sha a147945aae`. It was
already re-signed once during this session for benign drift. Expect it to be **stale again** —
`origin/main` has advanced at least to `d2dea317ec` since, and the epic's dependency set includes
`docs/config.md`, which drifts often.

## `bloated-shadeful-lamprey` — implemented but not landed

The only child with real work. Commit **`39c93ea3dc`** in worktree
`/Users/joeoakhart/lamprey-libwrites` (branch `lamprey-libwrites`), clean, parent `d2dea317ec`.
Splits `_lib_writes.py` 800 -> 378 / 280 / 231 by concern; proven **byte-identical** at the
top-level-block level; lint, typecheck, twelve `check_*` gates, the complexity `--lock` gate and
all four generators green. Remaining: CI selection re-run from clean (it was **stopped mid-run at
70% with zero failures** — treat as unrun), `tests/integration`, rebase, push, both +1s, submit,
close. Do not re-derive the split; read that ticket's HANDOFF comment first.

## Dependency order for the 11 unstarted children

Six are **roots** with no `depends_on` and can be worked in parallel — note that three of them
are size-relief prerequisites, so they unblock the feature work:

- `tasteful-historical-slug` — store-level project-to-repos mapping
- `microbial-dicey-milksnake` — store-compat capability registration
- `contrived-explicable-blobfish` — size relief: pagination cluster out of `fetcher`
- `reunitable-preodorous-quelea` — size relief: `update_one` sub-tree
- `bare-coed-thrasher` — size relief: STATUS cluster out of `reducer`
- `bloated-shadeful-lamprey` — size relief: `_lib_writes` (**done, awaiting landing**)

Then, in order:

1. `buried-genial-gyrfalcon` (needs slug, lamprey, thrasher) — tri-state `bridge_project`/`repos`
2. `algebraic-illstarred-mollusk` (gyrfalcon, blobfish) — multi-project inbound fetch
   and `blitheful-deceitful-warbler` (slug, milksnake) — legacy-store migration
3. `deathly-nondeadly-dorking` (gyrfalcon, quelea) — outbound dispatch + cross-project guard
4. `unworldly-narrow-iggypops` (gyrfalcon, mollusk, dorking, warbler, milksnake) — docs + ADR 0062
5. `gasolinic-microbian-puffin` — the live rehearsal; depends on **all 11**, so it is strictly last

Review plans in this order too: a review pins its direct dependencies' material, so reviewing a
dependent before its prerequisites wastes the LLM run.

## Recovery recipe — benign code drift (works WITHIN one environment)

When a claim fails with `the code the plan was reviewed against drifted: N dependency file(s)
changed (...)`:

1. `rebar review-plan <id> --status` — read-only, **no LLM**. Confirms `verdict: stale-code` and
   prints `verified_at_sha` and `currency_basis`.
2. `rebar sign-review <id>` — re-signs from the recorded REVIEW_RESULT sidecar with **no LLM
   re-run**, at current HEAD.

This is recovery, not a bypass: `sign-review` refuses when the **plan** changed, so it only ever
certifies across drift in files the plan did not depend on substantively. It was used twice this
session — once on lamprey (an attestation that PASSED but failed to persist, "generation remained
unstable after 3 attempts") and once on this epic (drift from `a147945aae` touching
`docs/config.md`). Try it before spending a full `review-plan`.

## The epic's claim belongs to the OUTGOING session

This epic is left `in_progress` **deliberately** — the work is genuinely underway, and its child
`lamprey` carries a real unlanded commit, so flipping the epic back to `open` would misrepresent
that. But the claim, the `claimed_session`, and the attestation's signing environment
(`ade0f2ef-51cc-45a2-bb97-c09846cd3df5`) all belong to a session that is ending.

The incoming session should **re-claim and re-cascade under its own environment**:

- Its verification of both this epic's and lamprey's attestations will return **`foreign_key`**,
  not `certified`. The claim gate fails closed on that, and **`sign-review` cannot fix it** — it
  re-signs from a sidecar but does not cross environments.
- So the new session must run a fresh `rebar review-plan 0e68-41eb-5782-4336` (and one for
  whichever child it claims) with `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1`. Both plans are settled and
  passed cleanly, so expect clean PASSes with no plan edits — budget the LLM time, not a rewrite.
- Do **not** reach for `claim --force` to paper over `foreign_key`. That bypasses the gate rather
  than satisfying it, and AGENTS.md scopes `--force` to a human operator's judgment call.

Nothing here is closed, and no code was pushed anywhere.

migration was rejected: four-figure event writes under the store lock, and the MCP-boot ensure entry
skips under lock contention, so it would silently skip there.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — mapping store, fetch fan-out, outbound dispatch, cross-project guard.
- `src/rebar/_store/ensures.py`, `_store/init.py` — the ensure unit seeding the mapping.
- `src/rebar/_store/compat.py` — the capability stamp.
- `src/rebar/reducer/`, `schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `_commands/composer.py`, `_lib_writes.py`,
  `_mcp_writes.py` — the two new ticket fields and their create-time arguments.
- `src/rebar/_cli/` — the `bridge projects` subcommand.
- `docs/` — the multi-project model, the mapping, an ADR.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge projects` lists, sets and removes project→repos entries on the store mapping, with the
      same operations on the library and MCP surfaces; per-surface test asserts each surface reads
      back an entry written by another.
- [ ] A store whose mapping holds two projects fetches both in a single pass and each ingested ticket
      records its source project; reconciler test asserts one JQL pair AND one enrichment pass
      (parent/comment/issuelink maps) per configured project, both projects' enrichment data present
      in the merged snapshot, and the recorded project on each created ticket.
- [ ] A ticket whose project is explicitly empty produces no outbound mutation; differ test asserts an
      empty mutation list for it while a sibling with a project produces one.
- [ ] A ticket created with an explicit project targets it rather than the repo default; dispatch test
      asserts the create call carries the ticket's project.
- [ ] An outbound update inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it still raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; paired applier test covers both directions.
- [ ] Every ticket in a pre-feature store resolves to the recorded legacy default with zero events
      written; migration test asserts byte-identical event count before/after the sweep.

      single-project store stays writable; store-compat test covers both, including that the

## Child decomposition (disjoint file sets)

- **Project mapping store** — `.bridge_state/projects.json` + helpers + ensure seed. Delivers
  migration/legacy-default criteria.
- **`bridge projects` command surface** — subcommand + library/MCP parity per epic `2f79`.
  Delivers criterion 1.
- **Ticket project field** — schema, CREATE data, reducer, create-time args on all three surfaces;
  promote-only rule (cannot change a bound ticket's project). Delivers empty-project criterion.
- **Ticket repos field** — schema, reducer, create-time arg, inbound defaulting from the mapping.
- **Multi-project inbound fetch** — `_build_snapshot` (fetcher.py) iterates the configured project
  set for the base JQL fan-out AND its three enrichment passes — `get_parent_map` /

  neither write). Ensure sweeps are convergence backstops for any residual divergence, not the

- **Docs + ADR** — model, mapping, tri-state field, decision record.
- **Live multi-project rehearsal** — LAST child: two live Jira Cloud projects on an isolated
  tickets-branch copy on the encrypted S3 remote (capability from epic `cf3c-1444-863e-49d7`);
